name: Roller-flank knuckle on the long dyad: a re-cut flank to lift the lead's drive-stroke wall (cx 43.75)

mechanism.notes: J1/K/J2/J3 O20 MR117-2RS; K slaved (clock-spring cap), never read; lobe ground into hub 2's cap ring -> bell crank (MR63ZZ pair, pin in link 1b, boss stacked on link 1b) -> bent long arm (3 mm Ti, straight run + arc concentric with hub K, 5-axis tip) -> MR63ZZ roller on an integral O3 Ti stub of the crank (retaining head O4.5 x 0.8 under the roller, sampled as metal) -> conjugate flank milled into a lateral boss of link 1a (5-axis / tilting-head wire EDM); pin knee (2 iglidur pins, sensed as the lead). Three merges vs the verified roller-flank row (lug into link 1a, lobe into hub 2's cap, roller pin into the crank): custom parts 15 -> 12. Rolling pairs: lobe-follower, roller-flank. Loops: drive, knee closure, K dyad stop. No rod, no ball links, 0 passive translations.

verdict: lever DEAD (measured): the long-stroke re-cut flank passes the law-only gate (kin360 0.7778, +13 poses) but cannot be parked - its flank boss sits on the deltoid (88-94 contact poses), lifting it takes the crank out of band, and every co-fit walks back to bk2 38-40.7 / dK_lim 42-47 (= the lead RSSR's 43). Best co-fit (short dyad, PA <= 43, stub head) worn frozen: 18.67 plain / 20.30 at 1 mm / 33.10 at 2 mm vs the lead 18.91 / 20.00 / 34.03, held out 23.73 vs 22.67 - level with the lead at cx 43.75 vs 49, not a lead change (< 1 point, worse held out and at 1 mm).
limiter: the skin, not the drive kinematics: a conjugate flank long enough for dK 55-57.5 at pressure angles <= 43 runs its contact from r 18 to 30 mm off hub K's axis (lug to 33 mm), onto the deltoid; frozen loss 99 of 360 = fold 88, slide 9, contact 2
